newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips give up gains to profit-takers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips give up gains to profit-takers.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks had skidded lower by midday Wednesday as investors took profits following a rally inspired by the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was off around 28 points at 7275, well below its exuberant session high of 7353. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was also softer, down 18/32 to yield 6.95 percent.
"We rose in a straight line for a long time, so it's normal to see consolidation," Dain Bosworth trader Frank Calta said.
Market watchers had predicted profit-taking would follow the initial bounce from the Fed rate decision.

Stocks were also distracted by a sell-off in bonds, knocked lower by data that showed the U.S. trade gap narrowed by 19.3 percent in March to $8.5 billion. A March deficit of $10.3 billion had been forecast.
The smaller deficit was attributed to record exports.
"The trade data is a factor for stock markets because, clearly, inflation can come from this area," said Ray Hirsch, director of the technology group at American Express Financial Advisors.
Hirsch said bonds were more nervous than stocks about prospects for inflation and perhaps had a predilection to weaken because they would have preferred to see the Fed boost interest rates.
Ron Doran, head of institutional equity trading at C.L. King and Associates, said the stock market is overbought and is prone to more profit-taking over the next few days.
"From now on investors will focus on economic data as it comes out and earnings," he said. "But for the short-term, the market is overbought."
On the Nasdaq composite, strong first quarter earnings at Dell Computer Corp, as well as Dell's announcement of a two-for-one stock split, boosted shares of personal computer makers.

Nasdaq eased from its session highs but was up around 10 points to 1374. Dell was up 7-7/8 to 107-1/2 after posting stronger-than-expected first quarter earnings of $1.08 per share versus $0.42 in the year-ago quarter.
Compaq Computer Corp rose six points to 102-1/4 while Gateway 2000 Inc added 3-3/8 to 74-1/2.
